newsitem.title: USA: US GDP seen up 3.5 pct in '97,3.0 pct in '98 - group.
newsitem.headline: US GDP seen up 3.5 pct in '97,3.0 pct in '98 - group.

text.p: The U.S. economy should grow 3.5 percent in 1997 and 3.0 percent in 1998, while consumer prices should rise 2.5 percent this year and 3.0 percent next year, the Conference Board projected Tuesday.

The Conference Board, a privately funded economic research group, forecast that in the near term, gross domestic product would expand at a 2.8-percent rate in the third quarter of 1997 as the Consumer Price Index (CPI) advances at a 2.6-percent rate.
"There is simply no sign of an interim cycle peak in activity," said Gail Fosler, senior vice president and chief economist at the Conference Board.

Relatively swift economic growth and a declining unemployment rate should push consumer price inflation above 3.0 percent during some periods of 1998, with food and energy prices adding to a rising core inflation rate, Fosler said.
However, rising industrial capacity and a strong dollar should help to limit inflation, she said.
"The key indicators -- inventories, bond yields, exports and the index of leading indicators -- are all favorable," Fosler said.

The report projected consumer spending would rise 3.1 percent in 1998, up from a projected 2.7 percent this year. In addition, she forecast the unemployment rate would fall to 4.6 percent in 1998 from 5.1 percent in 1997.
